decisions.decision: Possibility-toggling (forbid/permit) rides the BINARY requirement gate (checkRequirements + validatePlayerAction); strength-scaling rides the CONTINUOUS scoring channel (registerScoringContributor). They are physically separate code paths sharing one data record.
decisions.rationale: computeUtility is gate-independent (al.ts:447): a continuous score cannot make an action impossible, and a binary gate cannot express 'more attractive'. The code map explicitly warns conflating them yields 'scored but impossible' or 'possible but never chosen'. A forbidden action returns null in checkRequirements before scoring ever runs, so the two can never disagree.
decisions.rejected: A single 'affordance modifier' value in [-1,1] folded into computeUtility (would let a strongly-negative score masquerade as a gate but never truly remove the action from the possible set, breaking validatePlayerAction which has no scoring).

decisions.decision: The override gate is a UNIVERSAL engine-owned pre-target gate (shared function isAffordanceForbidden) called by checkRequirements, checkRequirementsReactive, AND validatePlayerAction — NOT a per-module REQUIREMENT_CHECKERS entry and NOT a POST_TARGET checker.
decisions.rationale: INV-16/17 bilateral parity: validatePlayerAction (al.ts:510) re-implements requirement iteration and does NOT call checkPostTargetRequirements (al.ts:323 is NPC-only), so any post-target override would silently skip the player. A REQUIREMENT_CHECKERS entry would work bilaterally BUT the engine owns this LAW (modules supply only the data on carriers, not the checker logic) — making it a pre-target engine gate keeps the law in the engine and the vocabulary in modules (INV-14).
decisions.rejected: Registering it as a normal module REQUIREMENT_CHECKER (works bilaterally but pushes the override-evaluation law into module space, and risks a module forgetting to register it); registering as POST_TARGET_REQUIREMENT_CHECKER (breaks player parity — al.ts:532 never iterates post-target).

decisions.decision: Overrides are STORED on the source (agent's AgentState or ZoneState) but EVALUATED target-centrically: when computing whether agent T may do action A, the engine collects overrides projected onto T from T-self + T's-zone + co-present projectors carrying match.targetId===T.
decisions.rationale: Storage-on-source gives the projector clean ownership of lifecycle/removal (mirrors how an agent owns its mood modifiers). Evaluation-on-target is required because the gate runs inside T's own checkRequirements/validatePlayerAction. Co-presence (perception.getCoPresent) bounds the cross-agent scan to the current location — cheap and spatially grounded.
decisions.rejected: A global override registry scanned for every (agent,affordance) pair (O(overrides) per check, no spatial bound); storing the override on the TARGET (projector loses ownership, removal becomes a cross-agent reach-in).

decisions.decision: Precedence when multiple overrides apply: any matching 'forbid' wins UNLESS a 'permit' override with a STRICTLY more specific match (affordanceIds beats categories beats tags beats minSeverity beats empty) targets the same action. Equal specificity: forbid wins (fail-safe-closed).
decisions.rationale: A zone curfew (forbid all violent, by category) that a personal power (permit this exact affordanceId) overrides is the canonical Type-II-vs-Type-I interaction. Specificity ordering makes 'a targeted exception beats a blanket ban' deterministic. Fail-closed on ties avoids a permit accidentally unlocking a base-game requirement the designer never intended.
decisions.rejected: Permit always wins (a stray permit could unlock anything); strength-weighted resolution (strength is a SCORING concept per DEC-1, must not leak into the binary gate); last-registered-wins (non-deterministic across save/load ordering).

decisions.decision: 'permit' overrides only LIFT the engine's universal possibility gates and the override-forbid gate — they do NOT bypass module REQUIREMENT_CHECKERS or post-target checkers unless the override explicitly lists those via a future opt-in. permit's scope is the affordance-SPACE (possible set), not arbitrary requirement nullification.
decisions.rationale: Keeps permit bounded and safe: a power that 'enables an action' enables it against base affordance gates and zone forbids, but does not magically satisfy 'isInvestigator' or 'maxWitnesses'. Prevents permit from becoming a god-mode that voids all module rules. Module-realizability target only needs permit to override forbid and base requirements, which this covers.
decisions.rejected: permit nullifies ALL requirement checkers (turns any power into rule-immunity, uncontrollable blast radius); permit does nothing but un-forbid (too weak — can't model a power that grants an action the base game forbids by period/requirement).

decisions.decision: The override gate runs in checkRequirementsReactive too (the reactive path that deliberately skips the mood gate), because a forbid is a hard possibility constraint, not a mood-relaxable preference.
decisions.rationale: Reactive evaluation relaxes mood because event urgency overrides a bad-mood reluctance (al.ts:342). But 'this action is impossible right now' (zone curfew, suppression power) is categorically different from 'I'm not in the mood' — urgency cannot make an impossible action possible. Skipping the override gate reactively would let a forbidden action fire on reaction.
decisions.rejected: Skipping the override gate in the reactive path (would let suppressed/forbidden actions leak through on event reactions — a correctness hole).

decisions.decision: Strength scaling from a relationship that does not exist yields 0 contribution (no auto-seed); modules opt into a fallback explicitly. Belief-confidence scaling inherits the 0.1 floor (beliefs.ts:115).
decisions.rationale: Matches computeUtility's existing null-relationship semantics (al.ts:461-464 → 0). Auto-seeding a relationship row as a side effect of a strength read would mutate state during a read and pollute the relationship graph. The belief floor means 'no belief ⇒ ~0.1·weight' not exactly 0 — documented so modules don't assume a true zero.
decisions.rejected: Auto-defaulting missing relationships to a 0.3 sentiment like getTestimonyWeight (mutating-on-read or surprising non-zero strength for strangers).

decisions.decision: Overrides are NOT conserved and expose NO transfer API (unlike attributes' transferAttribute). They are projected/removed, not moved.
decisions.rationale: transferAttribute (world.ts:707) is conservation-oriented for gold/HP. 'Transferring' a possibility-override between agents is nonsensical and would be a footgun (the same risk the code map flags for personality traits). A projector adds an override targeting another agent; it does not give away its own.
decisions.rejected: A transferOverride conserved-move API (no coherent semantics).

decisions.decision: Zone state is a NEW parallel mutable store (World.zoneStates: Map<locationId, ZoneState>), separate from the static LocationDef config, reusing the ScalarAttribute primitive for zone attributes.
decisions.rationale: LocationDef (world-types.ts:24) is immutable world-config (id/name/connections/isPublic) with no state field and is not iterated by the tick loop. SPEC 2's 'zone as active object of reality' has literally no home today. A parallel state map keyed by location id, lazily created, gives zones first-class mutable state without polluting config, and reuses the exact deformation math agents use (zero new physics).
decisions.rejected: Adding mutable fields onto LocationDef (mixes config and runtime state, breaks the world-editor which writes LocationDef verbatim); modeling a zone as a hidden Agent (zones aren't agents — would wrongly enter volition/perception/movement loops and the isPlayer-guarded paths).

decisions.decision: The plasticity seam is a one-directional, optional engine callback (onAffordanceOverrideUsed) carrying the override's opaque plasticityTrigger blob; the engine never reads the blob's fields.
decisions.rationale: INV-14: the engine must not know an override 'costs a piece of yourself' (that's the Negation/trauma module concept). Forwarding an opaque trigger to SPEC 1's registered consumer keeps the law (using a power can re-set you) generic and the meaning (how much, which axis) in module data. Optional trigger = a free power costs nothing.
decisions.rejected: Engine directly calling a plasticity function (couples SPEC 2 to SPEC 1 in the engine, and bakes 'cost' semantics into the affordance layer).

synthesis.engineLaw: An agent's or a zone's STATE can override the SET OF POSSIBLE ACTIONS for a TARGET — forbid (remove) or permit (restore) — as registered data, evaluated through the SAME pre-target requirement gate that already governs every NPC and player action; possibility is binary (the gate), attractiveness is continuous (the scoring channel), and the two never mix. The engine owns the law (how overrides combine, decay, persist, and gate bilaterally); modules own all vocabulary (what an override means, what triggers it, what it costs). Using an override may, as opaque module-defined data, trigger a permanent personality plasticity shift — the engine forwards that trigger without ever knowing it is a 'cost'.

GATE / POSSIBLE-SET (Phase 1):
- forbid removes an action from the NPC possible set: register an affordance, add a forbid override matching it, assert checkRequirements returns null; remove → returns target again.
- permit restores a base-forbidden action (e.g. period-gated): assert checkRequirements null without permit, non-null with permit (DEC-5 scope: lifts engine universal gates + forbid only).

PRECEDENCE/SCOPE EDGE: permit does NOT satisfy a module REQUIREMENT_CHECKER (e.g. isInvestigator) — assert a permit override does not bypass a registered module gate (DEC-5).
SCORING (Phase 2):

synthesis.reportMd:
# SPEC 2 — Affordance-Space Modifier: Canonical Diamond Design

## What this is
A genre-neutral engine primitive: an agent's or a zone's STATE can override the SET OF POSSIBLE ACTIONS for a target (self / another agent / a zone of co-present agents), as pure registered data. The engine evaluates these through the SAME requirement gate that already governs NPC and player actions. The engine never contains the words Negation/trauma/wound/debt — those are module data.

## Code-grounded findings (verified against source)
- **Single bilateral gate exists already, but is split**: `checkRequirements` (al.ts:304) and `validatePlayerAction` (al.ts:510) both iterate `REQUIREMENT_CHECKERS`, but `validatePlayerAction` does NOT call `checkPostTargetRequirements` (al.ts:323). So the override gate MUST be a shared *pre-target* engine function (`isAffordanceForbidden`) called by both paths + the reactive path — never a post-target checker. This is the linchpin of bilateral parity (INV-16/17).
- **No zone carrier exists**: `LocationDef` (world-types.ts:24) is static config (id/name/connections/isPublic), held as `readonly locations: LocationGraph` (world.ts:126), not iterated by the tick loop. A zone-as-active-object needs a NEW parallel `World.zoneStates: Map<locationId, ZoneState>`, reusing the `ScalarAttribute` primitive (attributes.ts) so zones get the same deformation math as agents with zero new physics.
- **Deformation/lifecycle idiom is reusable verbatim**: `AttributeModifier`/`MoodModifier` share an identical remaining/duration/decay model and a splice-on-expiry decay (attributes.ts:61, world.ts:592). Overrides reuse this exact idiom — no new lifecycle machinery.
- **Tick loop is bilateral** (world.ts:561 iterates all agents incl. player): override decay hooks here for agents; zones need a separate small loop (not agents).
- **Scoring vs gate are physically separate** (computeUtility al.ts:447 is gate-independent): possibility-toggling rides the binary requirement gate; strength scaling rides `registerScoringContributor` (al.ts:439). Conflating them is the central error avoided (DEC-1).
- **Strength-scaling reads exist**: `beliefs.getMaxConfidenceFor` (beliefs.ts:82, floor 0.1 at :115), raw `relationships.getRelationship().sentiment`, `getAttributeValue` (attributes.ts:94). Module supplies the keys; engine stays neutral (INV-14).

## Design in one line (engine law)
Forbid/permit overrides on agent-or-zone STATE re-shape the possible set for a target through one shared pre-target gate; possibility is binary, attractiveness is continuous, the two never mix; using an override may trigger a permanent plasticity shift via an opaque forwarded blob (SPEC-1 seam).

## Invariant proof
- **INV-06** (mood single-writer): untouched — overrides are a separate carrier; no direct mood mutation.
- **INV-14** (engine/module boundary): override records carry only module strings (source/category/match); the engine evaluates structure, never vocabulary; `plasticityTrigger` is opaque. Architecture test greps engine for forbidden strings + a synthetic-module probe.
- **INV-16/17** (bilateral): ONE `isAffordanceForbidden` consulted by NPC, reactive, AND player paths → no split-brain; player is fully gateable as override target.
- **INV-21** (default-on-load): all new fields optional; old saves load to empty → zero behavior change; omit-when-empty keeps the identical-output round-trip test green.

## Phasing (each independently tsc-0, test-green)
1. Gate + agent self-override (realizes Type-I). 2. Strength scaling + scoring. 3. Zone carrier (ZoneState, reused ScalarAttribute). 4. Cross-agent + plasticity seam (realizes Type-II + SPEC-1 bridge).

## Conflicts resolved
10 numbered decisions (DEC-1..10). Key ones: gate-vs-score separation (DEC-1); engine-owned universal gate not a module checker (DEC-2); store-on-source / evaluate-on-target (DEC-3); specificity precedence, fail-closed on ties (DEC-4); permit scope bounded to possibility space, not requirement-nullification (DEC-5); gate runs reactively too (DEC-6); zone as parallel state store, not Agent and not on LocationDef (DEC-9); plasticity via opaque one-way callback (DEC-10).

## Module-realizability
The Negation world is fully expressible after Phase 4 as pure module data: Type I = self `permit` override + `plasticityTrigger`; Type II = cross-agent/zone `forbid` with `strengthScale.fromSelfBelief`/`fromSentimentToTarget`; 'no one does both' = a module rule about which overrides carry triggers vs scales. Engine contains zero Negation/trauma vocabulary.

## Files touched (paths)
- NEW: C:\Ledevia\Projects\CLWA\packages\engine\src\affordance-modifier.ts
- EDIT: packages\engine\src\al.ts (tags field; 3× isAffordanceForbidden insertion; reason string)
- EDIT: packages\engine\src\agent-types.ts (AgentState.affordanceOverrides; ZoneState)
- EDIT: packages\engine\src\world.ts (zoneStates map + World API; tick decay; toJSON/loadState; WorldSaveAgentData/WorldSaveData; onAffordanceOverrideUsed)
- REUSE (unchanged): attributes.ts, beliefs.ts, relationships.ts, perception.ts, event-registry.ts

verdicts.lens: INV-14 GENRE-NEUTRALITY of both engine layers (Personality Plasticity + Affordance-Space Modifier)

findings.issue: SPEC 1 open-axis registry is only HALF-open: the engine's three trait-CONSUMPTION paths are hard-closed to the 6 OCEAN+H keys, so a module-registered axis (e.g. 'stability'/'wound'/'devotion') is unreachable by the very systems that make traits matter. registerTraitAxis lets a module DECLARE an axis, but nothing in the engine can SCORE, GATE, or DESCRIBE it. This breaks the locked OPEN-axes decision and the module-realizability target (a 'wound'/'devotion' axis is the whole point of the Negation world).
findings.evidence: al.ts:30 `export type OceanHTrait = 'O'|'C'|'E'|'A'|'N'|'H'` — AffordanceWeight.trait (al.ts:33) is typed to this closed union, so computeUtility (al.ts:451 via TRAIT_MAP al.ts:391, keyed `Record<OceanHTrait, keyof bigFive>`) can only score the 6. al.ts:134 resistTraits is a closed union `'openness'|...|'honesty'`. cg-engine.ts:342-347 checkTrait reads `(agent.profile.bigFive as unknown as Record<string,number>)[traitName]` — the bigFive object literally has only 6 keys (agent-types.ts:1-8), so trait:'stability' returns undefined→false. The spec's report claims 'cg-engine.checkTrait is ALREADY string-keyed so it reads module axes natively' — FALSE: it reads the closed 6-key profile.bigFive SEED, never agent.state.attributes['trait:...'].
findings.fix: The spec must extend the open-axis read path through ALL consumers, not just add Agent.trait(): (1) widen AffordanceWeight.trait to `OceanHTrait | string` (or add an optional `axis?: string` alt-field) and make computeUtility fall back to agent.trait(w.trait) for non-OCEAN keys; (2) redirect cg-engine.checkTrait to read agent.trait(traitName) (state axis → seed → undefined) so module axes AND plastic shifts are visible to CG rules; (3) keep resistTraits' typed union for OCEAN but add an open `axis?: string` escape hatch (instinct-builder.ts:198 already takes resistTraits generically). Without all three, registerTraitAxis is decorative.

findings.issue: SPEC 1's open-axis registry conflicts with two existing boot-smoke tests that hard-assert the closed 6-trait validTraits set. A module that registers a new axis and references it from a CG rule or resistTrait (the intended usage) will FAIL the suite — i.e. the 'quality bar: bun test green' is violated the moment a module actually USES an open axis.
findings.evidence: boot-smoke.test.ts:316-327 `validTraits = new Set(['openness',...,'honesty'])` asserts every affordance.resistTraits[].trait ∈ that set. boot-smoke.test.ts:495-504 does the same for CRIME_CG_RULES `{op:'trait'}` conditions against `validTraits = ['openness',...,'honesty']`. These iterate MODULE data, so the engine compiles fine, but a module exercising the new axis breaks them.
findings.fix: The spec's test-plan must add a phase step: replace the hardcoded validTraits literals in boot-smoke.test.ts with `new Set(getTraitAxes().map(a => a.key-or-OCEAN-alias))` so the validity check is driven by the open registry, not a frozen list. Call this out explicitly in SPEC 1 phasing (it currently omits any change to boot-smoke.test.ts).

findings.issue: Engine-seeded OCEAN+H is defensible BUT the spec under-states a genuine neutrality asymmetry: the engine bakes OCEAN psychology into non-registry code (baseMood derived from neuroticism/extraversion; loneliness scaled by extraversion; social-stress from neuroticism/agreeableness/honesty; fixed OCEAN+Enneagram prose). A truly unrelated genre cannot REMOVE or REPLACE these — they are unconditional. SPEC 1 routes traits through agent.trait() but leaves these derivations reading the same 6 axes, so the engine still 'knows' a specific 6-factor model, not merely 'seeds' it.
findings.evidence: world.ts:1988 `baseMood = saved.baseMood ?? (0.3 - bigFive.neuroticism*0.4 + bigFive.extraversion*0.2)`. world.ts:578 loneliness `-(LONE_RATE*(bigFive.extraversion*1.5+0.5))`. world.ts:536-538 social-stress `bf.neuroticism*1.5 + (1-bf.agreeableness)*0.5 + (1-bf.honesty)*0.3`. personality-prose.ts:4-50 fixed OCEAN+Enneagram prose. genre-neutrality.test.ts:137 explicitly blesses this as 'pure OCEAN+H psychology' = engine-universal.
findings.fix: This is a PRE-EXISTING design stance (OCEAN+H as a universal psychometric primitive, test-blessed) and is acceptable — but the spec MUST state it as an explicit scoping boundary rather than implying full openness. Add a decision note: 'OCEAN+H is an engine-universal psychometric primitive (precedent: genre-neutrality.test.ts:137); module axes are ADDITIVE channels for scoring/gating/prose, but the engine's built-in mood/stress derivations remain OCEAN-coupled by design. A genre that wants none of OCEAN simply seeds all 6 to 0.5 and ignores them.' Otherwise the 'could an unrelated genre use this unchanged' test is failed silently by the baseMood/loneliness/stress couplings.

findings.issue: Open-axis registry deviates from the established fully-module-seeded registry pattern without acknowledging it. Every other open registry in the engine (INTENT_KINDS, event categories, action verbs, requirement checkers) is seeded ENTIRELY by modules; registerTraitAxis is the lone registry the engine pre-populates. This is justifiable but the inconsistency should be documented so a future auditor doesn't 'fix' it by moving OCEAN seeding to a module (which would re-break computeUtility/personality-prose).
findings.evidence: event-registry.ts:899-905 INTENT_KINDS — empty map, modules call registerIntentKind (topic-engine.ts:77 '[REMOVED: built-in topic sources moved to modules]'). event-registry.ts:103 registerEventCategory — module-driven. Contrast: SPEC 1 has the engine seed 6 axes at boot.
findings.fix: Add one line to DD-PP-04 rationale: 'Unlike INTENT_KINDS/event-categories (fully module-seeded), the trait-axis registry is engine-seeded for OCEAN+H because computeUtility/personality-prose/baseMood are engine-resident consumers of exactly those 6 — moving the seed to a module would orphan those consumers. This asymmetry is intentional.'

findings.issue: SPEC 2's AffordanceOverride carries genre-neutral STRUCTURE but its example `source` values in the spec/report ('curfew', 'power_use') are domain strings — fine in modules, BUT the spec proposes the engine ship a built-in scoring contributor (affordanceOverrideScoringContributor) and a reason string in validatePlayerAction. The reason string is the only real leak risk: it must be generic. The spec already says 'Action not currently possible' (good), but does not flag that the existing architecture test's STRONG/CRIME_PROSE regexes are NOT the binding constraint — the binding constraint is INV-15 (no SCREAMING_CASE module-string fallback) and the No-Text-Matching guard. Verify the built-in contributor never branches on override.source/category string values.
findings.evidence: architecture.test.ts:303-315 flags `?? 'SCREAMING_CASE'` fallbacks; al.ts:445 clearScoringContributors isolation. The spec's built-in contributor reads `permit`-override strength — if it ever did `if (ov.category === 'power') ...` it would leak. The spec's API section also floats an optional /api/debug/affordances/:id route in routes.ts (server layer, not engine) — acceptable, but must not echo override.source into engine code.
findings.fix: Add an explicit invariant to SPEC 2: 'the built-in affordanceOverrideScoringContributor and isAffordanceForbidden MUST treat source/category/match.* as opaque strings — zero `=== <literal>` comparisons against them; matching is structural (set membership in match.affordanceIds/categories/tags, numeric minSeverity) only.' Add to the architecture test a probe: a synthetic module registers a forbid override of a brand-new category and isAffordanceForbidden honors it with zero engine edits (the spec lists this in testPlan — promote it to a hard gate).

findings.issue: SPEC 2's match.minSeverity couples the genre-neutral override layer to AffordanceDefinition.severity, whose ONLY documented engine meaning is 'for witness reactions' (a perception/crime-adjacent concept). Using severity as a generic ordering key for forbidding 'all violent actions' silently imports the assumption that higher severity == more-restrictable. An unrelated genre (e.g. a puzzle/dialogue game) may not populate severity meaningfully, making minSeverity matches behave arbitrarily.
findings.evidence: al.ts:97 `severity: number; // 1-10, for witness reactions`. It is a required field on every AffordanceDefinition but its semantics are witness-reaction-tuned, not a universal restrictability scale.
findings.fix: Either (a) document that minSeverity matching reuses severity as a pure numeric ordering with no semantic claim (and that genres not using severity simply omit minSeverity clauses), or (b) prefer match-by-`tags`/`categories` as the primary genre-neutral selector and demote minSeverity to a documented convenience. Lean (a) + a one-line caveat in the AffordanceMatch doc — low cost, removes the hidden assumption.

findings.issue: Both specs lean on a 'self-belief confidence' seam, but beliefs are keyed by SUBJECT (who the belief is ABOUT), not by HOLDER. The engine wrapper passing selfId as `subject` is correct ONLY if modules actually create beliefs with subject===self. The engine stays neutral (matcher + subject supplied by module), so INV-14 holds — but the specs' prose ('self-belief') could mislead a module author into thinking the engine has a self-belief concept.
findings.evidence: beliefs.ts:82-90 getMaxConfidenceFor(subject, matcher) filters `b.subject !== subject` — subject is the belief's object-of-attribution, not its bearer (the bearer is the BeliefManager owner). beliefs.ts:115 floors confidence at 0.1 only after decay.
findings.fix: Reword both seam docs from 'self-belief confidence' to 'confidence of beliefs the bearer holds whose SUBJECT the module designates as self (selfId passed as the subject arg)'. Keep the 0.1-floor caveat both specs already note. No code change — documentation precision to prevent module misuse.

verdicts.reportMd:
# INV-14 Genre-Neutrality Stress Test — Both Engine Layers

**Verdict:** Both designs are *mostly* genre-neutral and well-grounded in the real code, but SPEC 1 has a **load-bearing flaw** that defeats its own locked "OPEN axes" decision, and several leak-adjacent assumptions in both specs need explicit scoping.

## What holds up (verified against source)
- **Naming is clean.** Every proposed engine identifier (`PlasticityRule`, `applyPlasticShift`, `trait:`/`pp:` prefixes, `AffordanceOverride`, `isAffordanceForbidden`, `forbid`/`permit`, `zoneStates`, `plasticityTrigger`, etc.) was run against the live architecture-test regexes (`STRONG`, `CRIME_PROSE`, `TRADE_PROSE` in architecture.test.ts:123/164/206) — **zero trips**. No Negation/trauma/wound/debt/crime/trade vocabulary in the proposed surface.
- **Reuse claims are real.** `ScalarAttribute` (attributes.ts) + `driftAttribute`/`decayAttribute` run on EVERY attribute every tick (world.ts:591-592), so the anneal-for-free and persistence-for-free claims are accurate. The `attributes` save path (world.ts:1892, 1992-2004) has the SL-07 NaN defense the spec cites, so `trait:`/`pp:` keys round-trip with zero new save/load code.
- **SPEC 2's bilateral-gate reasoning is correct.** `validatePlayerAction` (al.ts:510-562) iterates only `REQUIREMENT_CHECKERS` (al.ts:532) and never `POST_TARGET_REQUIREMENT_CHECKERS` / `checkPostTargetRequirements` — so DEC-2 (override gate must be a shared *pre-target* engine function, not a post-target checker) is the right call for INV-16/17 parity.
- **SPEC 2's zone justification is correct.** `LocationDef` (world-types.ts:25) is static config (id/name/connections/isPublic), no mutable state, not in the tick loop — a parallel `zoneStates` map is genuinely the only home for a stateful zone.
- **Seam primitives exist as claimed.** `getCoPresent` (perception.ts:55), `getMaxConfidenceFor(subject, matcher)` (beliefs.ts:82), the 0.1 confidence floor (beliefs.ts:115), raw `getRelationship().sentiment` — all real.

## Where neutrality actually breaks

### SPEC 1: the open-axis registry is only HALF-open (MUST-FIX)
`registerTraitAxis` lets a module *declare* `'stability'`/`'wound'`/`'devotion'`, but **every consumer that makes a trait matter is hard-closed to the 6 OCEAN+H keys**:
- `computeUtility` scores via `TRAIT_MAP: Record<OceanHTrait, keyof bigFive>` (al.ts:391, 451) — `AffordanceWeight.trait` is the closed union `OceanHTrait` (al.ts:30,33).
- `cg-engine.checkTrait` reads `profile.bigFive` (cg-engine.ts:342-347) — the literal 6-key seed object (agent-types.ts:1-8), **not** `state.attributes['trait:...']`. The spec's report claim that checkTrait "reads module axes natively" is **false**; `trait:'stability'` returns `undefined → false`.
- `resistTraits` is a closed OCEAN+H string union (al.ts:134).

So a module axis is unreachable by scoring, CG gating, and resistance prose — i.e. exactly the channels the Negation world needs for a `wound`/`devotion` axis. **The fix must widen all three consumption paths**, not just add `Agent.trait()`.

### SPEC 1: existing tests block actual open-axis use (SHOULD-FIX)
boot-smoke.test.ts:316-327 and :495-504 hard-assert the closed `validTraits` set for `resistTraits` and CG `{op:'trait'}` conditions. The engine compiles, but the first module that *uses* a new axis fails the suite. Spec phasing omits any change here — it must drive `validTraits` from `getTraitAxes()`.

### SPEC 1: OCEAN-coupling in non-registry engine code (SHOULD-FIX, scoping)
`baseMood` from neuroticism/extraversion (world.ts:1988), loneliness from extraversion (world.ts:578), social-stress from neuroticism/agreeableness/honesty (world.ts:536-538), and fixed OCEAN+Enneagram prose (personality-prose.ts:4-50) are unconditional. This is a **pre-existing, test-blessed stance** (genre-neutrality.test.ts:137 calls it "pure OCEAN+H psychology" = universal) and is acceptable — but the spec must STATE it as an explicit boundary, not imply full openness. A genre wanting none of OCEAN seeds all 6 to 0.5 and ignores them.

### SPEC 2: opaque-string discipline must be an invariant (MUST-FIX, preventive)
The override layer's structure is neutral, but the spec proposes an engine-shipped scoring contributor and a `validatePlayerAction` reason string. These must NEVER `=== <literal>` against `source`/`category`; matching must be purely structural (`match.affordanceIds`/`categories`/`tags` set membership + numeric `minSeverity`). Promote the spec's own "synthetic-module override of a brand-new category honored with zero engine edits" test from testPlan to a hard architecture gate.

### SPEC 2: minSeverity smuggles a perception assumption (SHOULD-FIX)
`AffordanceDefinition.severity` is documented as "1-10, for witness reactions" (al.ts:97) — a perception-tuned scale, not a universal restrictability ordering. `match.minSeverity` reuses it as a generic "forbid all severe actions" key, importing the assumption higher==more-restrictable. Document it as a pure numeric ordering with no semantic claim, and prefer `tags`/`categories` as the primary neutral selector.

## "Could an unrelated genre use these unchanged?" — answer
- **SPEC 2: YES**, after the opaque-string invariant is pinned. The forbid/permit-on-state primitive carries no domain semantics; a puzzle game's "this door is sealed until you hold the key" is a `forbid` override scaled from a `fromAttribute` clause — no engine edit.
- **SPEC 1: NOT YET.** As written, an unrelated genre can declare a custom axis but cannot score, gate, or describe with it (half-open registry), and cannot escape the built-in OCEAN-coupled mood/stress derivations. After widening the three consumption paths + driving the test validTraits from the registry + documenting the OCEAN-coupling boundary, it reaches YES.

## Bottom line
No outright crime/trauma/Negation **vocabulary** leaks into either engine design — the static guards all pass. The genuine INV-14 failures are **structural**: SPEC 1's openness is cosmetic until the OCEAN-closed consumer paths are widened, and both specs have hidden domain assumptions (severity-as-restrictability; OCEAN-coupled mood math) that must be made explicit scoping decisions rather than silent couplings.

findings.issue: Belief-scaling math is built on a false premise: getMaxConfidenceFor returns 0 (not 0.1) when the agent holds NO matching belief, so magnitudeScale/resolveOverrideStrength can silently ZERO the entire shift/strength.
findings.evidence: beliefs.ts:81-89 — getMaxConfidenceFor: `let max = 0; ... if no match returns 0`. The 0.1 floor both specs cite ('floored at 0.1 at beliefs.ts:115', 'never 0') is in decayBeliefs (beliefs.ts:115) and only floors the confidence of an ALREADY-EXISTING belief during day-decay — it never runs for a non-existent belief. SPEC-1 seams.B and SPEC-2 §1.3/DEC-7 both assert the 0.1 floor makes 'no belief ⇒ zero strength' false; that is incorrect.
findings.fix: Correct both specs: with `fromSelfBelief`/`magnitudeScale` reading getMaxConfidenceFor, absence of any matching belief yields a literal 0 multiplier → a multiplicative scale must START from `step` (or `strength`) and ADD belief-weighted bonus, NOT multiply, OR the module must supply a floor. Concretely: resolveOverrideStrength must compute `base + weight*confidence`, not `base * (weight*confidence)`, and magnitudeScale must default to 1.0 with belief as an additive bonus. Document that a pure-multiplicative belief scale with no belief = dead rule (a real footgun for module authors).

findings.issue: SPEC-1 Seam A claim is false: the tick-phase handler context carries NO per-tick event stream, so the PP evaluator cannot 'match ability-use events visible without new plumbing'.
findings.evidence: event-registry.ts:670-690 TickPhaseContext exposes {agents, eventStore, gameMinute, processEvent, discoveries, approaches, sceneResidues, locations, goalManager, npcHomes, addMoodModifier} — there is NO `events` array of this-tick events. world.ts:1369-1382 builds tickCtx with exactly those fields. SPEC-1 seams.A says the evaluator 'reads the per-tick event/approach context' and 'ability-use events are visible without new plumbing (event-registry.ts:670-690)'. They are not — `approaches` is an OUTPUT array handlers PUSH to, and eventStore is the full historical store (scanning it every tick for all agents is O(agents × events) and grows unbounded).
findings.fix: Either (a) add a `recentEvents: WorldEvent[]` (this-tick window) to TickPhaseContext and populate it in _handlePhaseHandlers, OR (b) make event-driven plasticity fire from the event-processing path (processCascade/handleEventForGoals) rather than the tick-phase sweep — i.e. evaluate threshold rules when the matching event is processed, not by re-scanning eventStore. The spec must pick one and stop claiming zero new plumbing.

findings.issue: cg-engine.checkTrait key-convention mismatch: the spec says it 'is ALREADY string-keyed so it reads module axes natively' and would 'read state axis first', but it keys bigFive by FULL trait name while the new trait: axes are keyed by single-letter axis (trait:O). Redirecting it as written would never find the state axis.
findings.evidence: cg-engine.ts:342-346 checkTrait: `const traitName = cond.trait as string; const traitValue = (agent.profile.bigFive as ... Record<string,number>)[traitName]` — i.e. cond.trait is 'openness'/'honesty' (full key, matching keyof BigFive). SPEC-1 dataModel stores axes as attributes['trait:O'..'trait:H'] (single letter). SPEC-1 migration says redirect checkTrait to 'read state axis first, falling back to profile' — but state axis key is `trait:`+axisKey where axisKey∈{O..H}, NOT the full name. A naive `state.attributes['trait:'+cond.trait]` lookup ('trait:openness') would miss every seeded axis and silently fall through to the frozen profile seed — a split-brain (the exact failure DD-PP-03 claims to prevent).
findings.fix: Define ONE canonical axis-key space and a single name→axis map used by BOTH computeUtility (already uses TRAIT_MAP O→openness, al.ts:391) and checkTrait. Either store axes under the full name (`trait:openness`) so checkTrait redirect is trivial, or have checkTrait translate full name→single letter before the `trait:` lookup. The spec must specify the exact translation; as written it is a latent stale-trait bug in CG gating (which drives crime cascade behavior — oracle drift risk).

findings.issue: SPEC-2 threshold/precedence gate adds a per-affordance, per-decision O(co-present agents × overrides) scan to computeUtility's possible-set computation — the tightest hot path — and the spec under-states it as 'cheap'.
findings.evidence: volition.ts:154-165 loops `for (const aff of AFFORDANCE_REGISTRY) { checkRequirements(...) }` for EACH agent each decision. SPEC-2 wires isAffordanceForbidden into checkRequirements (al.ts:304) so it runs once per affordance per agent. isAffordanceForbidden (DEC-3, §1.5) must collect overrides from self + zone + 'any OTHER agent co-present with T' — i.e. a getCoPresent scan (perception.ts:54-65 is O(allAgents)) PLUS, for each co-present projector, a scan of its affordanceOverrides for targetId===T and a match-clause AND-test, PLUS DEC-4 specificity sort. Net per decision ≈ affordances × (allAgents + projectors×overrides×matchClauses). With A affordances and N agents that is O(A·N) per agent per decision → O(A·N²) per full proactive sweep. The spec calls co-presence 'cheap and spatially grounded' but never bounds N or caches the co-present set.
findings.fix: Hoist the co-present projector collection OUT of the per-affordance loop: compute, once per (agent, decision), the set of overrides projected onto this agent (self + zone-of-location + co-present cross-agent), then isAffordanceForbidden(aff,...) just match-tests against that pre-built small list. This drops the inner cost from O(A·N) to O(N + A·overrides). Add a fast-path: if the agent's location has no ZoneState and no co-present agent carries any affordanceOverrides, isAffordanceForbidden returns false in O(1) (the universal crime/economy case where zero override data exists). Spec the early-out explicitly.

findings.issue: Per-tick decay+drift over agent attributes is multiplied by SPEC-1's new axes: every agent gains 6 trait: axes + N pp: accumulators that all enter the Object.values(attributes) decay/drift loop every 5 minutes — for axes that, by default (irreversible, no anneal), have NOTHING to do.
findings.evidence: world.ts:589-593: `if (agent.state.attributes) for (const attr of Object.values(agent.state.attributes)) { decayAttribute(attr,5); driftAttribute(attr,5); }`. Today most agents have ~0-1 attributes (index.ts:728-739 seeds gold on a few). SPEC-1 seeds 6 trait axes on EVERY agent + player (Phase 1) plus a pp: accumulator per active threshold rule. decayAttribute iterates modifiers (trait axes normally have none → cheap) and driftAttribute early-returns when no drift — so the cost is small per axis, but it is now Object.values() allocating + iterating 6+N entries per agent every tick where it used to iterate ~1. At MMO scale (target) this is a real constant-factor regression on the timer.
findings.fix: (a) Skip the loop body for axes with no modifiers AND no drift — driftAttribute already early-returns, but decayAttribute still iterates an empty modifiers array and Object.values still allocates. Consider iterating Object.keys/for-in or maintaining a separate 'has-decayable-state' dirty set so axes that are pure frozen bases (the default irreversible trait) are skipped. (b) Do NOT seed pp: accumulators eagerly; create them lazily on first trigger (the spec's accumulation mode needs none at all). Spec the lazy-create to keep the steady-state loop at ~the current size for worlds with no active threshold rules.

findings.issue: pp: accumulator stored as ScalarAttribute base with max=Infinity has no decay path (decayAttribute only ticks modifiers, not base) — so a threshold rule that never crosses leaves a monotonically growing base, and SL-07's createAttribute re-clamp on load does nothing for an Infinity max.
findings.evidence: attributes.ts:60-69 decayAttribute mutates only attr.modifiers (base untouched). SPEC-1 dataModel stores accumulators as base (min=0,max=Infinity). The 'threshold: reset accumulator on cross' is the ONLY thing that lowers it; sub-threshold accumulation grows base forever. world.ts:1995-1996 loads with createAttribute(a.base,a.min,a.max) which clamps to [0,Infinity] = no-op. There is no NaN risk (finite guard at :1995) but there IS an unbounded-growth + 'never forgets' semantics the spec doesn't call out: 'accumulation' erosion and 'threshold' build-up never fade unless the module sets anneal/drift on the accumulator.
findings.fix: Spec must state: threshold accumulators that should fade between events MUST carry a decay mechanism. Since base doesn't decay via decayAttribute, either (a) store the accumulator as a single decaying MODIFIER instead of base (then decayAttribute fades it for free, matching the elastic model), or (b) require modules to set anneal/drift toward 0 on the accumulator. Pick (a) — it reuses the existing decay path and avoids the unbounded-base footgun.

findings.issue: computeUtility (al.ts:451,457) reading agent.trait('H')/trait('O') instead of the direct struct field adds a Map/object lookup + fallback-chain branch per weight per affordance per decision on the hottest path; the spec treats the swap as free.
findings.evidence: al.ts:448-454 loops `for (const w of aff.weights) { agent.profile.bigFive[TRAIT_MAP[w.trait]] }` — a direct property read today. SPEC-1 replaces it with agent.trait(axis) = `attributeEffective(state.attributes?['trait:'+axis]) ?? profile.bigFive[map] ?? 0.5`. attributeEffective (attributes.ts:54-58) sums modifiers and clamps; 'trait:'+axis allocates a string key each call; the ?? chain branches. Per decision that is weights×affordances×agents string concatenations + clamps. al.ts:457 also calls trait('H') for moodCurve every computeUtility. Functionally fine, but it converts a field read into a string-keyed object lookup + arithmetic on the tightest loop.
findings.fix: Precompute the agent's effective trait vector ONCE per decision (not per affordance): build a small {O,C,E,A,N,H:number} snapshot from trait() at the top of the volition per-agent block and pass it into computeUtility, so the inner weights loop reads plain numbers. Avoid `'trait:'+axis` string allocation in the hot loop by interning the 6 axis keys as constants. This keeps Phase-0 byte-identical AND avoids the constant-factor hit.

findings.issue: SPEC-2 reactive-path gate (DEC-6) runs isAffordanceForbidden inside evaluateReactiveVolition's per-reactor × per-affordance loop, compounding the cross-agent scan onto the event-driven path that already fans out per affected target.
findings.evidence: volition.ts:227-263 reactive loop: `for (const npcId of reactors) { for (const aff of AFFORDANCE_REGISTRY) { ... checkRequirementsReactive(...) } }`. SPEC-2 DEC-6 + §2.1 add isAffordanceForbidden to checkRequirementsReactive (al.ts:333). Each event can have many reactors (affectedTargets + object + subject), each re-running the co-present override scan. On a CG cascade that fires many events, this is reactors × affordances × co-present-scan per event.
findings.fix: Same hoist as the proactive fix: build the per-reactor projected-override list once before the affordance loop. Confirm the reactive path also benefits from the O(1) early-out when no override data exists (the crime/economy oracle case), so DEC-6's correctness (forbid holds reactively) costs nothing when no module registers overrides.

findings.issue: SPEC-2 zone-override gating needs zone state inside isAffordanceForbidden, but AffordanceContext has no World reference; the proposed ctx.zoneOverridesFor closure must be added at every ctx-construction site or the gate silently sees no zone overrides on some paths.
findings.evidence: al.ts:152-176 AffordanceContext has agents/locations/npcHomes/... but no World or zoneStates. buildAffordanceContext (world.ts:1772) is the main builder, but ctx objects are ALSO partially constructed in tests (genre-neutrality.test.ts:100 casts `{} as AffordanceContext`). If zoneOverridesFor is optional (spec uses `?:`), a path that forgets to set it makes zone curfews silently not apply — a correctness hole that won't fail tsc.
findings.fix: Add zoneOverridesFor (and the co-present projector source) to buildAffordanceContext at world.ts:1772 — the single production chokepoint — and make isAffordanceForbidden treat absence as 'no zone overrides' deterministically. Document that the player-action path (server.ts:237, routes.ts:1056) and reactive path (world.ts:258) all go through buildAffordanceContext, so one edit covers them; flag that any future hand-built ctx must set it.

findings.issue: validatePlayerAction skips checkPostTargetRequirements (confirmed), which the spec correctly routes around by making the override gate PRE-target — but the spec should also confirm the player path's witness/sentiment post-target gates remain NPC-only, i.e. the override gate must not be the only thing standing between player and an action an NPC would be post-target-blocked from.
findings.evidence: al.ts:510-562 validatePlayerAction iterates only REQUIREMENT_CHECKERS (pre-target, :532) and never calls checkPostTargetRequirements (al.ts:280, called only from checkRequirements:323 and checkRequirementsReactive:352). SPEC-2 DEC-2 correctly makes isAffordanceForbidden pre-target for this reason. No bug in SPEC-2 here, but it is worth an explicit test that an override forbidding the player composes correctly with the existing pre/post asymmetry.
findings.fix: Add to SPEC-2 test plan an assertion that a forbid override on the player trips validatePlayerAction at the pre-target stage with the new reason string, AND that removing it restores the player's existing pre-target-only validation behavior unchanged (no accidental post-target enforcement leaking onto the player).

findings.issue: INV-14 source-guard: the architecture lint scans engine source text; SPEC-1's `trait:`/`pp:` and SPEC-2's `forbid`/`permit`/`'agent'|'zone'` literals are universal and should pass, but the spec's own test plan greps for 'curfew' — which must live ONLY in tests/modules, not in any engine code comment/example.
findings.evidence: architecture.test.ts:1-60 reads engine .ts as text and (per its design) flags module-specific string literals; SPEC-2 testPlan says 'grep test: engine/src contains NO Negation|trauma|wound|debt|curfew'. The risk is purely that an illustrative comment in affordance-modifier.ts uses 'curfew' as an example (the spec's own §1.1 comment does: `e.g. 'power_use', 'curfew'`).
findings.fix: Ensure the NEW engine file affordance-modifier.ts uses only abstract examples in comments (e.g. 'a zone restriction', 'a projected restriction') — never 'curfew'/'power'/'Negation'. Trivial, but the spec's example comments would currently fail the spec's own grep test.

verdicts.reportMd:
# Adversarial Stress Test — Lens: HOT-PATH Performance + Correctness

Both designs are architecturally sound and the reuse-of-ScalarAttribute / shared-gate strategies are correct. But several load-bearing claims are **wrong against the real code**, and two hot-path cost claims are under-stated. Verified against source below.

## MUST-FIX (correctness — these break as written)

### 1. The 0.1 belief-confidence floor does not exist on the read path (both specs)
`getMaxConfidenceFor` (beliefs.ts:81-89) returns **0** when no matching belief exists. The `Math.max(0.1, …)` at beliefs.ts:115 is inside `decayBeliefs` and only floors an **already-existing** belief during day-decay. Both SPEC-1 (Seam B) and SPEC-2 (§1.3, DEC-7) assert "confidence floored at 0.1, never 0, so 'no self-belief ⇒ zero strength' is false." That is backwards. With a purely multiplicative `magnitudeScale`/`resolveOverrideStrength`, an agent with no matching belief gets a **0 multiplier** → the rule/override silently does nothing. Fix: belief must be an **additive bonus** over a base of 1.0 (or `step`), not a multiplier — or modules must be told a no-belief multiplicative scale is a dead rule.

### 2. SPEC-1 Seam A "no new plumbing" is false — no per-tick event stream exists
`TickPhaseContext` (event-registry.ts:670-690, built at world.ts:1369-1382) has **no** this-tick `events` array. `approaches` is an output buffer handlers push to; `eventStore` is the full history (re-scanning it per tick per agent is O(agents×events), unbounded). The PP evaluator cannot "see ability-use events without new plumbing." Fix: add a `recentEvents` window to TickPhaseContext, OR fire threshold rules from the event-processing path (processCascade / handleEventForGoals) instead of a tick sweep.

### 3. cg-engine.checkTrait key-convention mismatch → silent split-brain in CG gating
`checkTrait` (cg-engine.ts:342-346) keys `bigFive` by **full name** (`openness`); SPEC-1 stores axes as `trait:O`…`trait:H` (single letter, per `TRAIT_MAP` al.ts:391). The migration's "redirect checkTrait to read state axis first" would look up `trait:openness`, miss every seeded axis, and fall through to the frozen profile seed — exactly the split-brain DD-PP-03 claims to prevent. Because CG drives crime cascades, this is **oracle-drift risk**. Fix: define ONE canonical axis-key space + a shared name→axis map used by both computeUtility and checkTrait; spec the exact translation.

### 4. SPEC-2 gate cost on the tightest loop is under-stated
`computeUtility`/`checkRequirements` run per-affordance × per-agent × per-decision (volition.ts:154-165). `isAffordanceForbidden` (DEC-3/§1.5) must scan self + zone + **co-present projectors** (getCoPresent is O(allAgents), perception.ts:54-65) inside that loop → O(A·N) per agent → **O(A·N²) per proactive sweep** at MMO scale. Fix: hoist the projected-override set to once-per-(agent,decision); add an **O(1) early-out** when the agent's location has no ZoneState and no co-present agent carries any override (the universal crime/economy zero-override case). Spec the early-out explicitly.

## SHOULD-FIX (perf regressions / latent footguns)
- **5.** Per-tick `Object.values(attributes)` decay/drift loop (world.ts:589-593) grows from ~1 entry/agent today to 6 trait axes + N accumulators on **every** agent — for axes that, by default (irreversible), do nothing. Skip frozen/no-modifier axes; lazy-create `pp:` accumulators.
- **6.** `pp:` accumulator stored as ScalarAttribute **base** never decays (decayAttribute only ticks modifiers) → unbounded growth / "never forgets". Store the accumulator as a decaying **modifier**, not base, to reuse the elastic decay path.
- **7.** `computeUtility` swapping the direct `bigFive[…]` field read (al.ts:451,457) for `agent.trait(axis)` adds `'trait:'+axis` string-alloc + attributeEffective clamp + ?? chain per weight per affordance per decision. Precompute the 6-trait vector **once per decision**; intern axis keys.
- **8.** SPEC-2 reactive gate (DEC-6) compounds the cross-agent scan onto the per-reactor × per-affordance reactive loop (volition.ts:227-263). Same hoist + early-out.
- **9.** `AffordanceContext` has no World/zoneStates ref; the `zoneOverridesFor?` closure must be set at `buildAffordanceContext` (world.ts:1772, the single production chokepoint) or zone curfews silently no-op on some paths without tripping tsc.

## NICE
- **10.** Confirm player override composes with the pre/post-target asymmetry (validatePlayerAction never calls checkPostTargetRequirements, al.ts:510-562 — SPEC-2's pre-target DEC-2 is correct; add an explicit test).
- **11.** The new engine file must avoid the literal `curfew`/`power` examples the specs themselves use in comments — they'd fail the specs' own INV-14 grep.

## What checks out
- ScalarAttribute reuse, save/load free round-trip (world.ts:1892, 1992-2004 with SL-07 finite guards) — verified correct; trait:/pp: ride the existing attributes path with no new save code.
- driftAttribute/decayAttribute NaN defenses (attributes.ts:76-91) are solid; no NaN/clamp bug introduced by routing traits through them.
- `buildAffordanceContext` (world.ts:1772) is a genuine single chokepoint for the bilateral paths (proactive world.ts:1174, reactive world.ts:258, player server.ts:237 / routes.ts:1056).
- DEC-1 gate-vs-score separation is correct: a forbidden action returns null in checkRequirements (al.ts:321) before computeUtility (al.ts:447) ever runs — no "scored but impossible".
- Phase-0 byte-identical claim holds for the genre-neutrality test (genre-neutrality.test.ts:137-158 builds agents with bigFive and NO attributes → exercises exactly the trait() fallback path).
- Current scale is 8 agents / 8 locations; the O(N²) concerns are about the stated MMO target, not today's world.

findings.issue: SPEC-1 'XOR-boot' seeding claim is FALSE as written — the attributes/factions seeder at index.ts:728-742 runs UNCONDITIONALLY on every boot (it is inside createGameContext, which runs on both fresh boot AND loaded boot), then loadState overwrites. It is NOT guarded by `if (!savedData)`. The trait-axis seeder the spec wants to add 'mirroring the XOR-boot pattern' would therefore ALSO run on loaded boots. Safety only holds because loadState does a FULL REPLACEMENT (`agent.state.attributes = clean`, world.ts:2004). The spec's mental model ('fresh-seeder is SKIPPED on load') is wrong — nothing skips it.
findings.evidence: index.ts:728-742 (seeder, unconditional, inside createGameContext); index.ts:792-800 (createGameContext THEN `if (savedData) ctx.world.loadState`); world.ts:2004 (`agent.state.attributes = clean;` full replace, gated by `if (saved.attributes)` at 1992).
findings.fix: Rewrite DD-PP-08 to state the ACTUAL mechanism: seeding runs every boot but is harmless because loadState fully replaces `attributes` when `saved.attributes` is present. Then handle the gap in the next finding. Do NOT claim a `if(!savedData)` skip that does not exist; either add such a guard for the trait-seeder, or rely on full-replacement — but pick one explicitly and test it.

findings.issue: Old-save load SILENTLY WIPES freshly-seeded trait axes for any agent that has SOME attributes but no `trait:` keys. Because loadState does `agent.state.attributes = clean` (full replace) only `if (saved.attributes)`: an old save with `attributes:{gold}` (no trait keys, predates plasticity) replaces the freshly-seeded {gold, trait:O..H} with {gold} only — trait axes vanish. Reads still work via the profile-seed fallback in `agent.trait()`, so it is not data corruption, but it creates an INTRA-SAVE INCONSISTENCY: an agent with NO attributes block ('bob') KEEPS its seeded trait axes (the `if (saved.attributes)` block is skipped entirely), while an agent WITH a gold attribute LOSES them. Two agents in the same loaded world end up in different representational states (state-backed vs seed-fallback).
findings.evidence: world.ts:1992 `if (saved.attributes)` + 2004 full-replace; contrast save-load.test.ts:327-338 'empty state round-trips cleanly' (bob has no attributes → block skipped). Old millhaven saves carry `gold` on merchants (index.ts:738, world-loader.ts:286) but never `trait:` keys.
findings.fix: In loadState, after the `if (saved.attributes)` replace block, MERGE-seed any missing engine-owned `trait:`/`pp:` axes from profile.bigFive so every agent is uniformly state-backed post-load (or, conversely, decide trait axes are NEVER seeded into the attributes map and live only as lazily-created-on-first-shift — then the read accessor's fallback is the single source and the round-trip test stays vacuous for un-shifted agents). Add an explicit save-load test: load an OLD-style save (attributes:{gold}, no trait keys) and assert trait('O') === profile seed AND that the agent is in the chosen canonical representation.

findings.issue: SPEC-1 risks breaking the load-bearing 'toJSON → loadState → toJSON identical-output' round-trip test if trait axes are eagerly seeded for ALL agents. Today toJSON omits `attributes` when empty (world.ts:1892 `...(agent.state.attributes ? {...} : {})`), so bob serializes with NO attributes field and the identical-output + 'empty bob round-trips cleanly' tests pass. If Phase 1 seeds `trait:O..H` into EVERY agent's attributes (incl bob and the player), bob now always serializes a non-empty `attributes` block. The identical-output test (createTestWorld used for both worlds) may still pass IF both sides seed identically, but the player and any test agent built WITHOUT going through the server seeder (e.g. save-load.test.ts builds agents directly, never seeds trait axes) will diverge: world1 has no trait axes, loadState restores none, toJSON matches — but if any code path auto-seeds on construction, the two sides desync.
findings.evidence: world.ts:1892 omit-when-empty; save-load.test.ts:84-137 createTestWorld builds agents via `new Agent(profile, makeState(...))` with NO trait-axis seeding (seeding lives only in server index.ts:728); save-load.test.ts:149-163 identical-output test; :327 empty-bob test.
findings.fix: Keep trait-axis seeding OUT of the engine Agent constructor and OUT of makeState — seed ONLY in the server boot path (as the spec intends), so engine-level tests that don't seed stay byte-identical. Add a Phase-1 assertion to save-load.test.ts that a seeded agent's `trait:` axes round-trip AND that an UNSEEDED agent (bob-style) still produces zero `attributes` output. Confirm the player (index.ts:738 only seeds gold) is seeded with trait axes in the SAME fresh-boot block, else player toJSON shape differs fresh-vs-loaded.

findings.issue: SPEC-2 zoneStates restore has no clear-before-load and no reconstruct-into-existing safeguard. The spec adds `WorldSaveData.zoneStates?` and says loadState restores it, but loadState is called on a World that createGameContext may have already populated (boot reuses one World instance: createGameContext → loadState). Every other collection in loadState is explicitly cleared first (sceneResidues.clear() world.ts:1954, affordanceCooldowns.clear() :1938). If `this.zoneStates` is not cleared before restore, a zone seeded at boot but absent from the save persists as a stale zone (ghost curfew). Also: unlike agents, zones have no pre-existing map entries to gate on, so a corrupt/duplicate zone id in the save is admitted unguarded.
findings.evidence: world.ts:1931-1972 loadState clears _moodHistory/affordanceCooldowns/decisionCooldowns/sceneResidues before restore; index.ts:793-800 boot reuses the createGameContext World then calls loadState on it.
findings.fix: Spec must mandate `this.zoneStates.clear()` at the top of the zoneStates restore block (mirroring sceneResidues.clear()), then rebuild from the record with SL-07 finite-filtering on each zone's attributes (reuse the world.ts:1996 createAttribute re-clamp path) and affordanceOverrides (drop non-finite remaining/strength). Add a save-load test: a zone override present at boot but absent from the loaded save must NOT survive loadState.

findings.issue: SPEC-2 affordanceOverrides survive save/load but their RUNTIME EFFECT is partly dormant for the player. The spec's bilateral-parity proof rests on wiring isAffordanceForbidden into validatePlayerAction, but validatePlayerAction has NO live caller anywhere in packages/server or packages/modules — it is exported and referenced only in engine index + docs. So a forbid override targeting the player will round-trip in the save but will never actually gate a player action at runtime today. The save/load layer is fine; the bilateral guarantee the spec advertises is not currently reachable for the player.
findings.evidence: Grep for validatePlayerAction across packages: only definition (al.ts:510) + export (index.ts:57); routes.ts player paths (routes.ts:584/595) do not call it; the only affordance-driven route is debug force-affordance (routes.ts:1056) which is NPC-only via forceGoalFromAffordance.
findings.fix: Spec should flag (in the SPEC-2 phasing/INV-16 section) that player affordance gating is latent until a player-action endpoint that calls validatePlayerAction ships, OR scope the bilateral claim to 'the gate is in place; player parity activates when the player action pipeline is wired'. Add a test that calls validatePlayerAction directly with a forbid override to lock the contract even before a route exists.

findings.issue: World-editor + author-supplied `attributes` can COLLIDE with the engine-reserved `trait:`/`pp:` namespace. The seeder at index.ts:729 does `world.setAttribute(npcId, key, ...)` for every key in the NPC JSON `attributes` block (world-loader.ts:286 passes it through verbatim; editor writes NPC JSON verbatim, server.ts:152). Nothing stops an author from declaring `"trait:O": {base:0.9}` or `"pp:foo"` in the JSON, which would be seeded as a domain attribute and then be indistinguishable from / clobber the engine's plasticity axes. The world-editor offers a free-text '+ new' for open keys, so this is reachable by a careless author.
findings.evidence: world-loader.ts:286 `if (npc.attributes) startingAttributes[npc.id] = npc.attributes;`; index.ts:728-730 seeds them unconditionally via setAttribute; editor server.ts:144-156 writes NPC JSON with no key validation; editor app.js exposes attributes as open keys.
findings.fix: Spec must reserve the `trait:`/`pp:` prefixes explicitly: either (a) have the boot seeder reject/skip any author `attributes` key starting with `trait:` or `pp:` with a warning, or (b) add a world-data.test.ts assertion that no authored NPC `attributes` key uses the reserved prefixes. Document the reservation in world-loader and (ideally) make the editor refuse the prefix. Seed trait axes AFTER the author-attribute seeding so engine values win, or explicitly forbid the overlap.

findings.issue: SPEC-2 cross-agent overrides are stored ON THE SOURCE and evaluated via co-presence, but the SOURCE may be a DEAD or ABSENT agent after load. loadState restores `affordanceOverrides` onto every agent including dead ones; a forbid an agent projected onto a target persists on the (now dead) source's state and, per DEC-3, is collected when the target's co-present projectors are scanned. If the source died/exiled while the override has remaining>0, the cross-agent forbid keeps gating the target until decay. The save/load round-trip is correct, but the post-load reconstruction can resurrect an effect from a removed actor.
findings.evidence: agent-types.ts:142-160 AgentState (overrides stored on source); world.ts:1977 loadState sets alive/status from save but does not purge a dead agent's projected overrides; perception.ts:55 getCoPresent (filters by location/presence — a dead/absent source would not be co-present, but a DETAINED-yet-present source would).
findings.fix: Spec should specify override lifecycle on source state change: when an agent dies/becomes absent (and on load), its outbound cross-agent overrides with remaining>0 must be cleared or treated as inactive (gate isAffordanceForbidden should require the source to be alive+present, which getCoPresent partially gives only for the 'apart' case). Add a test: source dies → its cross-agent forbid stops gating the target after load.

findings.issue: routes.ts serializes the FROZEN seed `agent.profile.bigFive` (3 sites), so after a plastic shift the debug/intelligence UI shows pre-deformation values even though state is correct. Not a save/load corruption, but a post-load display inconsistency: a loaded save with a shifted trait:N renders the seed N in /api/debug and the player panel.
findings.evidence: routes.ts:118 `bigFive: agent.profile.bigFive`; routes.ts:801 `const H = agent.profile.bigFive.honesty`; routes.ts:819 `personality: agent.profile.bigFive`; routes.ts:654 venality from bigFive.honesty.
findings.fix: As the spec already lists under read-site migration, switch these to the effective `agent.trait()` / `world.getTrait()` reads so serialized personality reflects deformed state. Low priority for the save/load lens (state itself is correct) but needed for UI truth.

findings.issue: Strict save-version gate (`if (data.version !== 1) return null`) means any future need to bump the version (e.g. if zoneStates or trait representation ever requires a migration step rather than pure additive) will SILENTLY discard the entire save and start fresh, not migrate. Both specs are additive-optional today so version stays 1 and old saves load — but there is no migration shim if either spec later needs one.
findings.evidence: index.ts:283-286 `if (data.version !== 1) { warn; return null; }`.
findings.fix: No change needed for v1 of either spec (purely additive optional fields keep version 1). Spec should explicitly DOCUMENT that both layers MUST remain additive-optional (no required new fields, no type changes to existing fields) so the version-1 gate keeps loading old saves; if that ever stops being true, a migration branch (version 1→2) must be added rather than the current hard reject.

verdicts.reportMd:
# Adversarial Stress: SAVE/LOAD + World-Editor + INV-21

Lens applied to BOTH specs. I read the real code (world.ts toJSON/loadState, attributes.ts, agent-types.ts, server index.ts boot path, trait-randomizer.ts, world-loader.ts, world-editor server.ts + app.js, save-load.test.ts, al.ts gates, cg-engine.ts, genre/architecture tests). Verdict: the specs are largely sound on persistence REUSE, but three MUST-FIX issues center on the actual fresh-vs-loaded boot sequencing, which the specs describe inaccurately.

## What the specs got RIGHT (verified)
- Reusing `AgentState.attributes` for trait axes genuinely gives free round-trip: toJSON omit-when-empty (world.ts:1892), loadState SL-07 finite-filter + createAttribute re-clamp + drift preservation (world.ts:1992-2004) all already exist. INV-21 fallback (`if (saved.attributes)`) is real.
- World-editor edits ONLY the seed: server.ts:152 writes NPC JSON verbatim; app.js:376 edits `data.personality[O..H]`; world-loader.ts:229-235 maps `personality.{O..H}` → `profile.bigFive`. The editor never touches live state — SPEC-1's seed≠state claim holds. No editor change needed for v1.
- SPEC-2's pre-target shared-gate decision (DEC-2) is correct: validatePlayerAction (al.ts:510-536) re-implements requirement iteration and never calls checkPostTargetRequirements, so a post-target override WOULD skip the player. A pre-target shared `isAffordanceForbidden` is the right call. `buildAffordanceContext` (world.ts:1772) is a World method, so the proposed `ctx.zoneOverridesFor` closure has a clean wiring point.
- New engine literals (`trait:`,`pp:`,`forbid`,`permit`,`threshold`,`accumulation`) do NOT trip the architecture INV-14 grep, which targets crime nouns (architecture.test.ts:123/206). Adding a `Negation/trauma/wound/debt` grep is additive and sound. SPEC-1 plastic writes go through adjustAttributeBase (world.ts:674), not `.mood =`, so INV-06's mood-mutation guard (architecture.test.ts:278) is not tripped.

## The core defect (MUST-FIX #1 & #2): the 'XOR-boot' story is wrong
The spec repeatedly claims trait axes are 'seeded on FRESH boot, the fresh-seeder is SKIPPED on load'. That skip does not exist. The attributes/factions seeder (index.ts:728-742) is inside `createGameContext`, which runs on EVERY boot, fresh or loaded. The only reason loaded state survives is that `loadState` does a FULL REPLACEMENT of `agent.state.attributes` (world.ts:2004) — but ONLY `if (saved.attributes)` is present. Consequences:
- NEW save with shifted `trait:N`: survives (full replace). OK.
- OLD save with `attributes:{gold}` (no trait keys): the freshly-seeded trait axes are WIPED by the full replace → agent falls back to profile seed (reads OK) but is now state-less for traits.
- OLD save with NO attributes (bob): `if (saved.attributes)` is false → block skipped → bob KEEPS its seeded trait axes.
Net: two agents in the same loaded old save end up in DIFFERENT representations (state-backed vs seed-fallback). Not corruption (fallback saves reads) but an inconsistency the spec's design did not anticipate. Fix by choosing ONE canonical representation and enforcing it post-load (merge-seed missing engine axes, OR never eager-seed and rely on the accessor fallback as single source).

## SPEC-2 persistence gaps
- zoneStates restore needs an explicit `this.zoneStates.clear()` before rebuild (every other loadState collection clears first — world.ts:1938/1954); otherwise a boot-seeded zone absent from the save survives as a ghost. (MUST-FIX #4)
- Cross-agent overrides stored on a source that is dead/absent after load can still gate the target until decay; lifecycle on source-death/load is unspecified. (SHOULD-FIX)
- `validatePlayerAction` has NO live caller — the player affordance gate the bilateral proof depends on is dormant at runtime today; overrides round-trip but never gate a player action. (SHOULD-FIX)

## Reserved-namespace collision (SHOULD-FIX)
Authored NPC `attributes` keys flow verbatim through world-loader.ts:286 → index.ts:729 `setAttribute`. An author can write `\"trait:O\"` or `\"pp:x\"` in JSON (editor allows free-text open keys) and clobber engine plasticity axes. Spec must reserve the prefixes (boot-seeder skip + world-data test).

## Round-trip test exposure (MUST-FIX #3)
Keep trait-axis seeding out of the engine Agent constructor/makeState (seed only in server boot) so save-load.test.ts agents (built directly, never seeded) stay byte-identical and the 'empty bob round-trips cleanly' test (save-load.test.ts:327) keeps passing. Add Phase-1 tests for seeded-axis round-trip + unseeded-agent emptiness + old-save (gold-only) load.

findings.issue: DOUBLE-COUNTING via baseMood: the spec wants plastic shifts on trait axes (e.g. N/neuroticism) to be 'permanent disposition re-set', but baseMood is ITSELF a stored deformable scalar that was SEEDED from the SAME traits (N, E) and is NEVER recomputed from live traits. A plastic N shift therefore does NOT move baseMood (DD-PP-09 explicitly freezes baseMood at the profile SEED). Net effect: the central use-case ('trauma raises neuroticism -> agent is permanently gloomier') is SILENTLY A NO-OP on mood, because the only N->mood coupling that survives (social-stress ps factor) is a per-tick multiplier on negative-relationship pressure, not a baseline shift. The spec hand-waves this as 'a module wires N->baseMood explicitly' but never specifies the mechanism, and naive module authors will assume trait('N') shifts propagate to mood and be wrong.
findings.evidence: agent-types.ts:149 baseMood documented as 'Personality-derived mood baseline: 0.3 - N×0.4 + E×0.2'; index.ts:302 seeds it once; world.ts:1988 load-fallback re-derives from profile.bigFive (the SEED, not effective trait); world.ts:550/586 mood = baseMood + Σmods. DD-PP-09 in the spec: 'baseMood seed at :1988 keeps reading profile.bigFive ... a plastic N shift updates baseMood through an explicit recompute path ... NOT passively'. No such path is specified.
findings.fix: Specify the N/E->baseMood coupling concretely as an ENGINE-OPTIONAL but DEFINED mechanism, not a vague 'module wires it'. Either (a) make applyPlasticShift accept an optional 'derivedScalars' callback that the seeder also uses, so the SAME formula seeds baseMood at boot AND re-applies the delta on shift (single source of truth, no double-count); or (b) explicitly DOCUMENT in the spec that trait axes and baseMood are DECOUPLED by design and that mood-affecting plasticity must target baseMood directly via a separate plastic-baseMood path (see next finding). Pick one and write the formula; do not leave it to module authors to rediscover the 0.3-0.4N+0.2E coupling.

findings.issue: NO PLASTIC PATH FOR baseMood ITSELF, yet baseMood is the natural plastic target. The spec routes personality through ScalarAttribute 'trait:' axes but leaves baseMood as a bare number on AgentState (NOT a ScalarAttribute). So the engine has TWO permanent-disposition stores with INCOMPATIBLE physics: (1) baseMood = a raw clamped float with NO modifiers/drift machinery, mutated ad-hoc; (2) trait: axes = full ScalarAttribute base+modifiers+drift. A 'trauma permanently lowers baseline mood' rule cannot use applyPlasticShift (which only writes trait:/pp: attributes) — it would need direct baseMood mutation, which has NO finite-guard, NO clamp helper, NO onChange, and risks the exact INV-06 'direct write overwritten next tick' failure if done wrong (baseMood survives because the tick reads it, but any code that recomputes baseMood from traits would clobber it).
findings.evidence: agent-types.ts:149 baseMood:number (NOT ScalarAttribute, unlike attributes? at :154). attributes.ts deformation machinery only applies to ScalarAttribute. applyPlasticShift in the spec wraps adjustAttributeBase('trait:'+axis) — cannot target baseMood. world.ts:1988 shows baseMood IS re-derived on load-fallback, so it is conceptually trait-derived but mechanically frozen.
findings.fix: Decide explicitly: either MIGRATE baseMood into the attributes map as attributes['mood:base'] (a reserved key) so it joins the same deformation machinery and applyPlasticShift can target it — but then world.ts:550/586/1890/1988 and index.ts:302/307 must all read/write through attributeEffective, a real (rejected-by-DD-PP-02) refactor; OR add a parallel World.applyPlasticBaseMoodShift(npcId, delta) that finite-guards + clamps [-1,1] + fires onMoodChange, and state in the spec that baseMood is the legal plastic mood target while trait: axes are the legal plastic personality target. The spec currently implies trait plasticity is sufficient for mood-relevant trauma — it is not.

findings.issue: AMBIGUOUS ELASTIC/PLASTIC REGIME BOUNDARY ON A SHARED AXIS. The spec offers addTraitModifier (ELASTIC, springs back) AND applyPlasticShift (PLASTIC, permanent base set) on the SAME trait: axis, plus optional anneal (drift back toward a value) which makes a 'plastic' base shift ITSELF reversible. The boundary is therefore NOT clean: a shift with anneal is elastic-on-the-base (slow spring via drift), while a modifier with a long duration is elastic-on-top. Two different mechanisms produce indistinguishable observable behavior (a value that returns toward baseline over time), with NO rule for which to use. Worse: anneal writes ScalarAttribute.drift, but driftAttribute runs on the EFFECTIVE base every tick regardless of WHY the base moved — so a module that sets drift for annealing will ALSO drift any future plastic shift toward the same 'toward', silently coupling unrelated shifts on that axis.
findings.evidence: attributes.ts:35 drift is a single per-attribute field (one drift config per axis, not per-shift). attributes.ts:76-91 driftAttribute moves attr.base toward d.toward unconditionally. Spec ruleOrApiSchema: applyPlasticShift(..., anneal?) 'writes anneal.drift on first shift'. Because drift is axis-global, a second rule shifting the same axis with a DIFFERENT anneal.toward overwrites the first, or compounds — undefined.
findings.fix: Define the regime boundary as a hard rule in the spec: (1) ELASTIC = addTraitModifier ONLY (decaying modifier, base untouched) — use for temporary disposition buffs; (2) PLASTIC = applyPlasticShift moving base — use for permanent set; (3) ANNEAL is a property of the AXIS, not of a shift, so the spec must state that anneal is set ONCE at registerTraitAxis time (or first-shift), and DOCUMENT that all plastic shifts on an annealing axis converge to the same 'toward'. Forbid per-shift anneal divergence, or move anneal to TraitAxisDef. Also add a test asserting two plastic shifts with different anneal on one axis is rejected/last-wins-documented, not silently compounding.

findings.issue: LIVE TRAIT READS INSIDE THE MOOD TICK ARE NOT MIGRATED COHERENTLY, creating split-brain BETWEEN mood and personality even though the spec claims a single accessor eliminates split-brain. _computeMoodTick reads agent.profile.bigFive DIRECTLY (the immutable SEED) for the social-stress ps factor, every tick; loneliness reads bigFive.extraversion directly; moodCurve reads bigFive.honesty directly. The spec's migration list (DD-PP-03) says world.ts:536/578 switch to trait(), but world.ts:536 is INSIDE _computeMoodTick which is ALSO called by advanceMoodMath (calibration). If those reads switch to the deformed trait() while baseMood stays seed-frozen (DD-PP-09), then mood's BASELINE (baseMood, from seed N/E) and mood's PRESSURE terms (social-stress from deformed N, loneliness from deformed E) read DIFFERENT versions of the same trait — a genuine split-brain WITHIN the mood computation.
findings.evidence: world.ts:507-554 _computeMoodTick: ps = bf.neuroticism*1.5 + (1-bf.agreeableness)*0.5 + (1-bf.honesty)*0.3 reads profile.bigFive live; world.ts:578 loneliness reads profile.bigFive.extraversion live; al.ts:457 moodCurve(mood, bigFive.honesty). Spec proposes switching these to trait() but keeps baseMood frozen on seed — so N appears in mood both deformed (pressure) and frozen (baseline).
findings.fix: Make the decision explicit and consistent: EITHER (a) all trait reads that feed mood use trait() AND baseMood is recomputed from trait() through the defined coupling (finding 1's option a) so there is ONE N everywhere; OR (b) the mood subsystem's trait reads stay on profile.bigFive (seed) deliberately, and the spec states that mood is driven by the IMMUTABLE temperament seed while behavioral utility (al.ts:451 personalityScore) uses deformed traits — a defensible 'temperament vs character' split, but it MUST be written down, because silently mixing is the split-brain the spec claims to have killed. Add a test pinning which N each mood term reads.

findings.issue: CALIBRATION HELPER IS NOT SIDE-EFFECT-FREE w.r.t. mood, contradicting the spec's stated basis for DD-PP-02. The spec repeatedly justifies NOT unifying mood onto ScalarAttribute by citing that _computeMoodTick is 'also called by the side-effect-free calibration helper advanceMoodMath'. But advanceMoodMath DOES mutate agent.state.mood on every tick (it is how it builds the curve). If trait reads in _computeMoodTick switch to trait() and trait() reads deformed state, then running calibration (advanceMoodMath) on a save with plastic shifts will produce DIFFERENT mood math than the same NPC pre-trauma — calibration is no longer comparing apples to apples, and because advanceMoodMath writes state.mood, it LEAVES the agent's mood at the calibrated value (a real mutation), now influenced by deformed traits it was never meant to consider.
findings.evidence: world.ts:806-827 advanceMoodMath loops _computeMoodTick which writes agent.state.mood (world.ts:550). world.ts:551-553 comment claims it is 'side-effect-free' but that refers ONLY to skipping attribute decay; mood IS written. Spec DD-PP-02 rationale leans on this 'side-effect-free' framing.
findings.fix: Correct the spec's rationale: advanceMoodMath is side-effect-free of ATTRIBUTE decay, not of mood. Then decide whether trait() in _computeMoodTick is acceptable for the calibration path — if calibration must reflect un-deformed temperament, _computeMoodTick's trait reads should explicitly use the profile SEED (not trait()) and the spec should say so, OR advanceMoodMath should snapshot/restore state.mood. Do not leave the contradiction in the design doc.

findings.issue: 'pp:' ACCUMULATOR ATTRIBUTES RIDE THE SAME DECAY/DRIFT LOOP AS REAL ATTRIBUTES, which is the intended reuse, but with max=Infinity (per dataModel) a threshold accumulator that uses decayAttribute for 'cooling off' is fine, yet an accumulator is supposed to be a raw counter — if a module ever attaches a modifier or drift to a pp: key (nothing forbids it), the accumulator's effective value diverges from its base, and the spec's 'threshold crosses on base' logic (it resets base) will desync from any modifier-driven effective reading. Minor because no module would do this intentionally, but the engine does not guard it.
findings.evidence: world.ts:592 (real tick) iterates ALL attributes incl. any pp: key for decayAttribute+driftAttribute. dataModel stores accumulator as attributes['pp:<ruleId>'] min=0 max=Infinity base=accumulated. Nothing namespaces pp: out of the generic modifier/drift APIs (addAttributeModifier accepts any key).
findings.fix: State in the spec that pp: accumulators are base-only (no modifiers, no drift) and that the PP evaluator reads attr.base directly (not attributeEffective) for accumulators, while trait: axes read attributeEffective.
